Agent.description: A coding agent, by the name `--agents` and a project's settings take.

AgentsLine.description:
What an `agents` line says, as the toggles have it.

`{"type": "named", "agents": ["claude"]}` in JSON: tagged as a task is,
with the agents beside the tag, since a variant holding a list has no
field of its own for them to be named by.

oneOf.description: `agents --yes <agent>...`: exactly these.

`agents remove --yes <agent>...`: none of these, every one the
project names, which is how a line asks for no agent at all, since
naming none is not one. The command refuses it, with its own reason.

Asking.description:
An install of a plan that waits for somebody to say yes, an MCP server
from elsewhere than the library, as the install screen confirms one:
what it would give each agent of each project, laid out as its line
would say it ([`crate::install::foreseen`]), then the task that writes
it once that has been shown.

The task carrying the yes is handed over here, beside the lines it was
shown with, rather than the panel setting one on the task it holds:
which install waits for one is core's, and the yes is the
confirmation's alone. The panel sends it in the place of the task it
confirms, `task` by its place among the plan's.

confirmed.description: That task, saying yes: its line with `--yes`.

lines.description:
For each project it names, a line naming the install, then what
each agent there would run or reach, and each warning, as the
install screen's confirmation shows them.

task.description: Which of the plan's tasks it confirms, by its place among them.

Boxes.description:
How one entry in the registry stands with every offer ([`Offered`]):
what each of its boxes shows, told as the install screen tells it, by
[`install::survey`] and [`install::holding`], so the panel ticks the box
the screen ticks.

A box neither listed in `held` nor of a kind in `closed` is empty: the
project holds nothing of its name, and records no installation of it.
Only the boxes that are not are listed, a project holding a few of the
hundreds offered.

closed.description:
Each kind none of its boxes can be asked about, and why, by the code
a plan locks one by: every kind of an entry that opens no project,
and each a project has nowhere to put ([`install::receives`]), or
could not be surveyed for.

held.description:
Each box of a name it holds something of or records, kind by kind,
in the order of [`Snapshot::offers`].

Cancel.description:
What `POST /api/v1/tasks/cancel` is sent: the run to stop, by its number
as `command_started` told it, `{"run": 3}`.

By its number rather than "whatever runs now", so a cancel that crosses
the end of the run it was meant for never stops the one queued behind
it: by then that one has a number of its own. A field it does not have
is refused, as a task's is.

run.description: The run's number, as the events tell it.

Cancelling.description:
What a cancel is answered with: the run asked to stop and its lines,
`{"run": 3, "lines": [...]}`. Whether it stopped is for how it finishes
to say: a run past the point where it can stop runs to its end.

lines.description: Its lines, each as somebody would type it.

Caution.description:
What a command line takes away, which a front end asks somebody to
confirm before it runs the line: what [`cautions`] reads off the parsed
command, as [`refused`] reads a refusal, so a line is asked about the
same way whatever task it came from, and by every front end.

One list, here, rather than one per front end: the panel holds no rules
(D-18), so which of its lines need a yes first is said with each preview
it is answered with, in these words, and a list in TypeScript would be a
second place for a command to be forgotten. The TUI asks its own
questions, worded for the row they are about, before it builds a task.

Only what takes something away, or writes over somebody's work: a line
that only adds, or that changes what is installed where its agents now
read, is shown before it runs and runs once asked. And never a dry run,
which a line of a command that takes `--yes` is without it: it takes
nothing away, and says what it would.

oneOf.description:
`remove --yes`, at either level: the artifact deleted. And
`mindweaver export --yes`, which deletes from the folder it writes
what an earlier export put there and the library no longer holds.

`uninstall`, every form of it, and `mindweaver remove --everywhere
--yes`, which uninstalls from every project first.
`unlink`, at either level.

`unload`, at either level: `unlink`'s twin, for a loaded workspace,
whose copies in the projects are left orphaned.

`--force`: on `install` and `uninstall`, and on `update` that is
told `--yes`.

`mindweaver gather remove --yes`: a gathered source forgotten, what
it put on the shelf and its clone deleted, and what was installed
from it left in the projects, orphaned, as `unload` leaves a loaded
workspace's.

Cell.description:
One box of a selection: whether `project` should hold what `reference`
names, as `origin` offers it.

`{"project": "alpha", "reference": "skill:deploy", "origin": "workspace",
"wanted": true}` in JSON, which the panel sends: the project by its entry
as the workspace's marker spells it, as a snapshot lists it, the artifact
as a command line names it, and the origin as `--from` takes it, which
every listing prints. A field it does not name is refused, as a task's
is.

wanted.description: Whether the project should hold it from there: ticked, or not.

CellSent.description:
One box of a selection: whether `project` should hold what `reference`

`{"project": "alpha", "reference": "skill:deploy", "origin": "workspace",

as the workspace's marker spells it, as a snapshot lists it, the artifact
as a command line names it, and the origin as `--from` takes it, which
every listing prints. A field it does not name is refused, as a task's
is.

wanted.description: Whether the project should hold it from there: ticked, or not.

CliCode.description:
Every code the CLI gives of its own, for what went wrong: unique beside
core's and the local server's, and never renamed once given.

Closed.description: A kind none of a project's boxes of can be asked about, and why.

Confirm.description:
One thing a line of a task takes away, which the panel has somebody
confirm before it asks for the run: an item of a preview's `confirm`,
one for each [`Caution`] of each line ([`cautioned`]).

The words beside the word, so the panel says what a line takes in the
CLI's words rather than its own, and draws by the word alone.

line.description: Which of the preview's lines, by its place among them, from 0.

message.description: The same, said for whoever is asked.

Conflict.description:
Boxes of one name in one project that cannot all be as asked, and why:
none of them is planned, since which of them was meant is not something
to guess.

cells.description: Each box that clashes, as it was asked.

Contents.description: One file of an artifact, as a front end may show it.

file.description:
The file, as it was asked for: a route from the artifact's folder,
`/` separated, or a rule's own file name.

hash.description:
The SHA-256 of what it holds ([`hash::bytes`]), when it was read
whole: none for one larger than [`CAP`], which never is.

What `edit --if-unchanged` takes, so a front end that changes the
file holds the change to what it read, and is refused when somebody
changed it since (`edit_stale`). Hashed here, of the bytes the text
was read from, rather than by the front end from the text: one
recipe for every hash of a file, and a text a browser hashed could
be told apart from the file by nothing but a line ending.

manifest.description:
What it declares and says, cut as core reads it, when it is the file
the artifact is read from (a skill's `SKILL.md`, a rule's own file)
and its text was read; none for any other file, whose front matter
no agent reads as such.

text.description:
What it says, when it is UTF-8 text no larger than [`CAP`]; none
otherwise, and [`withheld`](Self::withheld) says why.

withheld.description: Why there is no text, when there is none.

CoreCode.description: Every code core gives, for what went wrong: unique across core, and never renamed once given.

Crumb.description: One folder on the way down to the one listed.

name.description: Its name, or the root's path for the root, which has none.

Declaration.description: One key of an artifact's front matter, and what it is given.

value.description:
A string as it is; anything else, a list or a mapping, a number or
nothing, as YAML writes it, so a value is shown whatever its shape
rather than only those the format defines.

Directory.description: Where a holder keeps one kind.

path.description:
A route from the holder, `/` separated, or the path itself when no
route leads there.

Does.description: What an update does with one installation.

Draft.description:
An artifact a command is about to write, as the panel asks core to judge
it ([`Query::Validate`]): tagged as a query is, `{"type": "add", ...}`.

oneOf.description:
What `add` would write, by the fields an `add` task carries: a
template by its name, as `--template` takes it, or for an MCP
server how it is started or reached, as `add mcp`'s options say it.

What `edit --contents` would write into the artifact `reference`
names, `kind:name`, given `text` whole: its `SKILL.md`, or a rule's
file.

What `edit` would write into the MCP server `name` told `server`,
how it is started or reached, by the fields an `edit_server` task
carries.

Drafted.description:
What `POST /api/v1/validate` is sent: a draft, and what it would be
written in ([`Query::Validate`]).

Entry.description:
One line of the action log.

What it serializes to is a contract, as a status report's is: each field
by its name, and the two that can quote a URL as a [`Redacted`], which
holds none. A row an older build wrote before the scrub still holds one
in the file until a command that writes opens the ledger, and is
redacted as it is read ([`history`](LedgerStore::history)).

at.description: When it happened, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

detail.description: What it said, successful or not, with every URL in it [`redacted`].

target.description: What the action was about: a URL, a name. A URL is [`redacted`].

EntryStatus.description:
One entry of an MCP server in one of a project's agents' config files,
and how it stands there: what the installed view lists of what it
received as entries rather than copies (D-23).

One an agent rather than one a server, as an installation's entries are
recorded: what Claude's `.mcp.json` holds of a server can be edited
while Codex's is not, and a foreign one is somebody's in one file alone.

agent.description: The agent whose config file it is in.

file.description:
That file, as a route from the project, with `/` whatever the
platform: the one the ledger recorded writing it into, or for a
foreign one the one the agent reads now (`Agent::mcp_file`).

name.description: The server's name, the key it is under.

origin.description:
Where what was installed came from, as `--from` takes it; none for a
foreign entry.

state.description:
How it stands, as an artifact's state says it: never `authored`,
which no entry is, and `foreign` for one nothing records.

Event.description:
One thing the panel is told.

Tagged by its name in snake_case beside its fields, as a task and a
query are: `{"type": "changed", "scopes": [...]}`.

oneOf.description:
Something a backend watches changed on disk, so what the panel shows
of each scope may be out of date: one event for every change the
watcher took in together, each scope once, in the backend's words.

A task's lines started to run on the writer thread, as run `run`:
counted from 1 in the order runs start, the number a cancel names
it by. With whether it takes a cancel, as the backend's preview
said ([`Preview::cancellable`]), so a panel offers one for a run
another tab or a script sent too.

[`Preview::cancellable`]: crate::Preview::cancellable

How run `run` is going, as the backend reported it
([`Underway::report`]): its own JSON, carried unread, as a changed
path's scope is.

[`Underway::report`]: crate::Underway::report

Run `run` was asked to stop (`POST /api/v1/tasks/cancel`), from
this tab, another or a script: whether it stopped, and where, its
finish and its outcome say. Told once, however often it is asked.

The writer thread is busy with run `run`, so whatever is sent now
waits its turn behind it: told when a run or a switch is queued
while a run is under way, and to a subscriber as it subscribes
while one is, with the run's latest [`Progress`](Event::Progress)
after it. With its lines, whether it takes a cancel and whether it
was asked to stop, as its start and any cancel said.
Run `run` stopped, however that went: the reply to the run says how.

The backend acts on something else since ([`Backend::switch`]),
and what it names is watched: everything is to be asked for again,
and nothing shown before kept, since it was of what it acted on
before. Told on the writer thread, once the switch is taken, to
every subscriber, the tab that asked for it among them
([`Events::switched`]), with how many switches were taken since the
bus was made, this one counted.

[`Backend::switch`]: crate::Backend::switch

The subscriber may have missed something: it has just connected, or
it fell behind. Everything is to be asked for again.

With how many switches were taken since the bus was made, as the
latest [`Switched`](Event::Switched) said: a subscriber that missed
one, a tab whose stream was let go while it was hidden or one that
fell behind, learns it from a count other than the one it heard last,
and lets go of what it shows of what the backend acted on before as
it would on hearing `Switched`. A count rather than a word that a
switch happened, which only a bus that knew what each subscriber had
heard could say.

Every path the backend named is watched, so a change to one arrives
as [`Changed`](Event::Changed).

Not every one is, so a change there arrives as nothing, and what the
panel shows is refreshed by hand: the system's limit on watches was
reached, or a watch could not be set up at all.

entry.description:
The workspace's entry for it, as the marker spells it; none for a

failures.description:

findings.description:

name.description: What its marker calls it; none for an entry that opens no project.

Files.description: Every file and folder of an artifact, as a front end may list them.

entries.description:

manifest.description:

Finder.description:
A skill directory a search can ask, by the word the marker and a

Finding.description:
One thing doctor found, as a report says it: what it is, by its code,

agents.description:
The agents it keeps something from, in report order: never empty

message.description: What is wrong, naming that path.

path.description: The file or folder it is about, absolute: the one the fix acts on.

Folder.description: One folder directly inside the one listed.

linked.description:
Whether the workspace links it, by the path an entry leads to, as

path.description: Where it is, absolute, as a request names it to list it in turn.

symlink.description:
Whether it is a link to a folder rather than a folder: listed and

FolderIs.description:
What a folder is, the strongest of what it holds: a mind project, a
weaver workspace, a git repository, or any other folder.

Folders.description:
One folder and the folders directly inside it, as a front end may offer
them to be chosen.

failures.description:
What it could not read or name, each with its code
([`BrowseFailure`]): a subfolder whose type will not read, or whose

folders.description:
Its subfolders, in the order of their names, hidden ones only when
asked for, and no more than [`FOLDERS_CAP`].

hidden.description:
How many of its subfolders are hidden, their names starting with a

home.description:
The home the front end was given, normalized, as a folder a request
may name, for a way back to it: none when there is none, or when it
is no such path ([`policy::path`]).

is.description: What it is itself, so it can be chosen as one of its subfolders can.

path.description: The folder listed, absolute, as it was asked for.

trail.description:
Each folder from the root down to it, it last: what a front end
offers to go up by, each by the path it is asked for by.

truncated.description:
Whether it holds more subfolders than [`FOLDERS_CAP`], which
`folders` stops at.

Found.description:
A directory a workspace could manage.

What it serializes to is a contract, as a status report's is: each field
by its name. The panel reads it in what a scan it asks for is answered
with, so it says its TypeScript too.

agent_files.description:
Each name at its root an agent reads something from
([`Agent::reads_at_root`], of every agent), in name order: what makes
a repository's reason [`Reason::Agents`], and listed for a mind
project too, which can hold them as well. Looked at, never followed
or read: a link there counts as what it is called.

id.description:
The id its settings name it by (D-09), whatever it is called and
wherever it is: none for a git repository that is not a project yet,
for a project a `mind.toml` still marks, which has none, and for one
whose marker would not open, which is a failure beside it.

linked.description: Whether the workspace links it already.

mind.description:
A mind project already, rather than a git repository that is not one
yet and would need `mind init` before it can be linked.

moved.description:
The entry it moved from, when it is not linked and holds the id the
workspace's ledger last saw at an entry where no project is any more
([`MindProject::is_vacant`]): spelled as `route` is, so `mindweaver
relink <moved> <route>` run there follows it. None otherwise, and for
an id another directory holds too, which is a copy rather than a
move.

reason.description: Why it is worth linking: the strongest of what it holds.

route.description:
What `mindweaver link` would be given for it, run where the request
spells routes from: the route from there, `/` separated, when it is
inside, and its path otherwise.

Given.description:
How an agent starts an MCP server, or reaches one: a program or an
address, never both.

In JSON, what a front end sends a command line's options as, and what
the snapshot says a definition is told as: tagged by `type` inside the
object, `{"type": "program", "command": "npx", ...}`, as a task is, each
pair as an array of its two words. A field it does not have is refused,
as a task's is: it is a write, and one misspelled would be dropped.
Every secret is the name of the variable it is read from, and no field
holds a secret's value, there being none for it to hold.

oneOf.description: A program an agent starts, `--command`.

arg_env.description:
Each argument read from a variable, after those written as they are
(`--arg-env VAR`). No secret: a program's arguments are what a
process list shows, and Codex reads no secret into one.

args.description:
What it is started with, in order (`--arg`), before every argument
read from a variable.

command.description: The program, as the agent finds it (`--command`).

env.description:
What its environment is given, each value as written (`--env
K=V`), before every secret.

secret_env.description:
Each variable passed on to its environment under its own name, a
secret (`--secret-env VAR`): the shape every agent can give one,
Codex's `env_vars` among them.

oneOf.description: A server at an address, `--url`.

bearer.description:
The variable `Authorization: Bearer` is followed by, a secret
(`--bearer-env VAR`): what Codex reads one into
(`bearer_token_env_var`).

events.description:
Whether it is reached over server-sent events rather than streamable
HTTP (`--sse`).

headers.description:
What every request carries, each value as written (`--header K=V`),
before every secret.

secret_headers.description:
Each header whose whole value is read from a variable, a secret
(`--secret-header H=VAR`): what Codex reads one into
(`env_http_headers`).

url.description:
Where the server is, as typed (`--url`): checked for a credential
before anything is written, since the file would keep one, and
never kept or said whole once one is found.

url_vars.description:
Each part of the address read from a variable, by the name the
address writes between braces where it goes (`--url-var NAME=VAR`).
No secret: an address is what a log or a proxy shows, and Codex
reads no secret into one.

GivenTo.description:
How one agent would be given an MCP server: what it cannot be given of
it, what its entry would run or reach, and what it asks before it
starts one.

dropped.description: What its entry would be written without, as `show` says it.

refused.description:
Why it would be given none of it, each by its code and in its
words: what it cannot be given at all, as `show` says it, or else

Held.description: One artifact a holder holds, and how it stands there.

agents.description:

issues.description:
Everything `validate` says of it, warnings included, each saying

origin.description: Where what was installed came from, as `--from` takes it.

state.description:

state.description:

ticked.description:
Whether the box is ticked ([`install::holding`]): the offer the

and none of one whose every copy has gone, for ticking it to put
them back.

repository.description: The repository it is in, as [`url::canonical`] spells it.

stars.description: How many stars its repository has, where a finder counts them.

folder's, or its repository's for one at the root.

path.description:
The folder in the repository it is in: none for the root, or where
no finder said, which a take gathers the whole repository from.

reference.description: The branch a finder named, none for the repository's default.

repository.description: The repository it is in, as [`url::canonical`] spells it.

stars.description: How many stars its repository has, where a finder counts them.

Holder.description:
Which level a task runs at: what holds the artifacts it is about.

`{"type": "project", "entry": "alpha"}` in JSON, or `{"type":
"workspace"}`: the shape a task's own variants have, which a variant
holding one string cannot take inside the object the tag is in.

oneOf.description: The workspace, for its own artifacts: `mindweaver <cmd>`.

A project, by its entry: `mind -C <entry> <cmd>`, or `mind <cmd>` for
the one at the root the commands run from.

A project whose own workspace is not the one on screen, by its entry:
`mind -W . -C <entry> <cmd>`, which names the one on screen, so a
change drops that workspace's record and an add takes its templates.

Still the project's command rather than `mindweaver <cmd> -p <entry>`,
which would consult the same workspace: a project's row teaches the
project's command, at every row alike, and `-W` only where leaving
it out would consult another.

HolderSent.description:
Which level a task runs at: what holds the artifacts it is about.

`{"type": "project", "entry": "alpha"}` in JSON, or `{"type":
"workspace"}`: the shape a task's own variants have, which a variant
holding one string cannot take inside the object the tag is in.

oneOf.description: The workspace, for its own artifacts: `mindweaver <cmd>`.

A project, by its entry: `mind -C <entry> <cmd>`, or `mind <cmd>` for
the one at the root the commands run from.

A project whose own workspace is not the one on screen, by its entry:
`mind -W . -C <entry> <cmd>`, which names the one on screen, so a
change drops that workspace's record and an add takes its templates.

Still the project's command rather than `mindweaver <cmd> -p <entry>`,
which would consult the same workspace: a project's row teaches the
project's command, at every row alike, and `-W` only where leaving
it out would consult another.

Judged.description:
What core says of a draft: what `validate` would say of it once written,
and why the command writing it would write nothing, when it would.

Each field by its name, a contract once a front end reads it, as a
report's are.

issues.description:
Everything `validate` would say of the artifact as it would be
written, warnings included, in its words: none when what would be
written cannot be told.

refused.description:
Why the command would write nothing, by the code and in the words it
would refuse with; none when it would write.

Kind.description: A kind of artifact, by the word a command line takes for it.

KindTargets.description: The folders a project's settings install one kind in.

folders.description: Each folder as the settings spell it, `/` separated.

KnownHere.description:
A workspace this machine knows, as `mindweaver workspaces` lists it, with
how the workspace a snapshot is of stands with it: whether it loads it,
and whether it could.

Beside the row rather than in it, as a shelf row's origin is
([`Shelved`]): the row is the machine's list, the same whichever
workspace asks, and what one of them loads is nothing that list says.
Told here rather than by a front end from `in_use`, `stale` and
[`Snapshot::loaded`], whose paths it would compare itself: two spellings
of one folder are one workspace, which only a comparison of where each
leads tells.

default.description:
The default workspace, in home: listed for being the default,
whatever its own `known` says.

in_use.description: The one in use where the list was asked for, as `resolve` chose it.

loadable.description:
Whether this workspace can load it: it opens, it is not this one,
this one loads it by no spelling yet, and its path is text a command
line can hold. What a front end offers to load, by its `path`, which
`mindweaver load` is given as it is.

loaded_as.description:
The entry this workspace loads it by, when it loads it, as
[`LoadedWorkspace::entry`] spells it: what `mindweaver unload` is given.
The first, when it loads it by more than one spelling.

name.description:
What its marker calls it; none for one that would not open, which has
no marker to read.

projects.description:
How many projects it links, each directory once, stale ones among
them: its own count, which says which of several weavers is which.

remembered.description:
Whether the default workspace's `known` names it, which is what
`mindweaver workspaces forget` takes out. False for the default itself,
and for the one in use when nothing remembers it.

stale.description:
Why it would not open, when it would not: listed rather than left
out, since a workspace that has gone is the one somebody has to find
to forget it.

Written through [`redacted`](crate::url::redacted), as an error's
message is in a [`Said`](crate::code::Said): a marker that does not
parse is quoted in its own words, a source's URL among them perhaps,
and whoever wrote that file is no promise that it holds no
credential.

stale_projects.description: How many of those would not open.

Library.description: The workspace's own artifacts, held as a project holds its own.

artifacts.description:
Each of its own, by kind and then name: no project's, so none
stands in a state, and nothing is installed into them.

directories.description: Where it keeps each kind, as a route from the workspace's root.

failures.description:
What could not be read in it and is no artifact's: a folder that
cannot be listed, its templates.

holders.description:
Each project its registry links that holds a copy of one of its own,
in the order of `artifacts`, then of the registry.

origin.description:
What `--from` takes for each of its own, and what an install of one
records as its origin: so a front end names it in a command line by
core's word rather than by one of its own that core could spell
differently.

servers.description:
Each of its own MCP servers whose definition reads, in the order
of `artifacts`, as each agent would be given it: what a page of
servers shows beside each one's row of `artifacts`.

LibraryHolder.description:
A project holding a copy of one of the workspace's own: one whose install
the ledger tells came from it ([`install::from_the_library`]), the rule
`mindweaver remove --everywhere` takes the copies it removes by.

Told here rather than by a front end comparing a copy's
[`origin`](Held::origin) with [`Library::origin`], which would be a
rule of its own, and a different one: a record from before origins were
kept names none, and is a copy of one of the workspace's own all the
same while no workspace it loads offers that name.

entry.description:
The project, as its registry entry spells it ([`Project::entry`]):
its artifact of that kind and name is the copy. Each entry that
spells one directory is a holder of its own, as each is a project
of the snapshot's.

kind.description: The one of the workspace's own it holds a copy of.

LibraryServer.description:
One of the workspace's own MCP servers, as `add mcp` would be told to
write it and as each agent would be given it.

Worked out here, from each agent's renderer, rather than by a front end
from the definition: what an agent runs is what its own entry spells
([`mcp::Runs`]), an input reaching Claude as `${VAR}` and OpenCode as
`{env:VAR}`, and what it cannot be given is core's report of it
([`McpDefinition::expressibility`]).

agents.description: How each agent would be given it, in report order.

given.description:
How it is started or reached, as `add mcp`'s options would say it
([`mcp::Given::of`]), for a form changing it to start from: none
when the definition holds what no option says, which is changed as
text.

Licence.description:
Where a gathered artifact says what it is licensed under, and what it
says.

Tagged by `from`, beside what that place said, so a reader tells a
licence its author declared from a line read off a file:
`{"from": "manifest", "text": "MIT"}`, `{"from": "file", "file":
"LICENSE.txt", "text": "Apache License"}`, `{"from": "plugin", "text":
"Apache-2.0"}` or `{"from": "unknown"}`.

oneOf.description:
The `license` its manifest declares, as written: a licence's name,
or words pointing at a file it bundles, as the Agent Skills format
has it.

A licence file in its folder, beside its manifest, which declares
none: the file's name, and its first line that holds anything, as
written, when there is one to read ([`KEPT`] characters of it at
most).

Neither, for a skill gathered from a plugin a marketplace lists
(#103): the licence the plugin declares, in its catalog entry or its
own `plugin.json`, as written, every skill of it under it unless the
skill says otherwise. Added after the rest.
None of those: nothing it holds says.

Listed.description: One file or folder of an artifact.

folder.description: Whether it is a folder, whose files are listed after it.

path.description:
Its route from the artifact's folder, `/` separated, as [`Contents`]
takes it; a rule's own file name. One whose name no route spells is
refused (`contents_name_unfit`) and listed by that name as near as
UTF-8 writes it, which another entry's can match: a refused entry is
shown, never asked for.

refused.description:
Why it is not followed, when it is not: a link leading out of the
holder, or back into a folder it is in, or something that does not
read. Listed all the same, since somebody looking for why a skill
misbehaves is looking for exactly that.

size.description:
How many bytes a file holds; none for a folder, and for one not
followed.

LoadedWorkspace.description: A workspace another one loads, and how much of its own it offers.

entry.description: The entry as the marker spells it: what `mindweaver unload` is given.

error.description: Why it would not open, when it would not.

name.description: Its name; none for one that would not open.

offers.description:
How many of its own it offers to install, counted from what the
install machinery offers, so the number is what an install shows. A
second spelling of one workspace offers what the first does.

origin.description:
What `--from` takes for what it offers, and what an install of one
of them records as its origin: the first spelling's, for a second
spelling of one workspace, as its offers are.

path.description: Where it points: what `mind unload` is given, from a project.

Locked.description:
A box whose change is not made, and why, by the code the change would be
refused with: `foreign` and `edited` as an install or an uninstall gives
them ([`Refused`]), or the error asking the project for it gave.

Manifest.description:
The file an artifact is read from, cut at its front matter as core cuts
it: what a front end shows as a table of what it declares above the
markdown it renders.

Cut here rather than by a front end from [`Contents::text`], since where
front matter ends, and whether a rule's fences hold any, are rules
([`frontmatter::split`], [`RuleManifest::read`]): a panel cutting it
itself could show as declared what every agent reads as content.

body.description:
What follows the front matter, as an agent reads it: the whole file
when no front matter is read.

front_matter.description:
Each key at the top of its front matter, in the order written, every
one the format does not define among them; none when it has none
core reads: no fences, fences that never close, or a block that is
no YAML mapping.

Mark.description:
One directory a front end marked, by the path a command is given, with
what to do to it: what [`Task::Marks`] holds, and [`Task::minds`] builds
a batch from. `{"path": "/home/you/blog", "change": "link"}` in JSON.

MarkSent.description:
One directory a front end marked, by the path a command is given, with
what to do to it: what [`Task::Marks`] holds, and [`Task::minds`] builds
a batch from. `{"path": "/home/you/blog", "change": "link"}` in JSON.

MarkerFile.description: The file inside `.mind` a project's marker is read from.

MindsChange.description:
What one directory's mark on the minds screen asks of the workspace, when
it differs from how the directory started: what [`Task::minds`] is built
from. By its name in snake_case in JSON: `"init_and_link"`.

oneOf.description:
`mind init` in it, then link it: a repository that is not a mind
project yet.

Missed.description:
One artifact a project received that some of its agents read nowhere,
and those agents.

agents.description:
The agents among the project's that read it nowhere, in report
order. Never empty.

Offered.description:
One thing there is to install, from one place: a row of the install
screen turned round by artifact, and of the panel's matrix (#79).

Told by core's own list of what an install offers ([`install::survey`]),
rather than put together by a front end from the library, the shelf and
the loads: only that list leaves out a name no copy can be filed under,
and reads what each loaded workspace offers, which nothing else in a
snapshot lists.

origin.description:
Where it is offered from, as `--from` takes it and an install of it
records it: what a box of it names its offer by.

summary.description: The one line a listing shows.

Outcome.description: What running a task's lines produced.

ok.description: Whether every line ran and found everything in order.

runs.description:
Each line that ran, in order: up to the first that failed, for a task
whose lines lean on each other ([`Task::chained`]).

Pending.description: One installation an update says something of.

copies.description:
The copies that names, each a route from the project, `/`
separated: put back, written over or left.

does.description: What an update does with it.

forced.description:
Whether a change reaches it only forced: a copy changed since it was
installed, which an update not forced leaves alone and, once nothing
offers it any more, an uninstall not forced leaves too. Said here so
a front end sends `--force` by core's word, rather than telling from
the state, the step, or both, which of core's refusals its change
would meet.

left.description:
Why an update leaves it as the project holds it, when it does
([`Left`]).

origin.description:
Where it came from, as `--from` takes it: none for a record from
before origins were kept.

state.description: How it stands, as `status` says it.

Place.description: Which of the three places offers something to install.

Planned.description:
What a selection the panel asked to plan amounts to ([`Query::Plan`]):
core's plan of it ([`install::Plan`]), each change in it the task that
runs it.

Tasks rather than core's changes, so the panel sends back what it was
handed, never a task it puts together itself: the `install` and
`uninstall` tasks, each a project by the entry its box named it by, which
the backend turns into the folder the registry resolves as it does any
task's. Sent as one `apply_install`, as the install screen applies its
marks, each line runs whatever came of the ones before.

asks.description:
Each of `tasks` that waits for a yes ([`install::asks_first`]), with
what it would give each agent of each project and the task carrying
the yes, in the order of `tasks`.

conflicts.description:
Boxes of one name in one project that cannot all be as asked, none
of which is planned.

locked.description:
Boxes whose change is held back, each by the code the command would
refuse it with, or why the project could not be asked about it.

tasks.description:
Each `install` and `uninstall` that carries the selection out, in
the order to run them. None carries a yes: an MCP server from
elsewhere than the library is only previewed by its line, until its
confirmation (`asks`) is sent in its place.

Preview.description:
What a task would run, worked out with none of it run: what
[`Backend::preview`] answers, and `POST /api/v1/tasks/preview` sends as
it is, `{"lines": [...], "confirm": [...], "cancellable": false}`.

cancellable.description:
Whether a run of it can be asked to stop while it runs (`POST
/api/v1/tasks/cancel`): one of its lines reports how it goes and
stops when asked, a gather, as only the front end can say of its
commands.

Said with the lines, so the server knows which run takes a cancel
from the moment it starts, the very preview it runs by, and refuses
one of a run that takes none (`uncancellable`) rather than pass on a
cancel that would do nothing; and so the panel knows to offer one
before the first step is reported.

confirm.description:
What the panel has somebody confirm before it asks for the run, one
item for each thing a line takes away; none for a task the panel
runs once it is asked to.

The backend's own JSON, carried to the panel unread, as a watched
path's scope is: which lines take something away is a rule of the
front end's, and so are the words for it. Said where the lines are,
so the panel is told it of the very lines it shows, rather than
asking a second time about a disk that may have changed between.
The server only carries it: a run sent without the panel having
asked anybody is run, as a shell runs the line typed into it, since
whoever holds the token is the person at this machine and the
question is for their slips, which is the panel's to ask.

lines.description: The command lines, each as somebody would type it.

Project.description: One entry in a workspace's registry, and the project it opens.

agents.description:
The agents its settings name, in report order: a slot each for every
artifact's own, so they line up.

artifacts.description:
Everything it holds, authored, received or somebody's, by kind and
then name, the rules its `AGENTS.md` block holds among them (D-23).

directories.description: Where it authors each kind, as a route from it.

entries.description:
Each entry of an MCP server its agents' config files hold, and each
one the ledger records writing, as `status` lists them: by agent,
then name, a foreign one among them (D-23).

entry.description:
The entry as the marker spells it, which `-p` and `unlink` take; none
for a project no workspace links.

failures.description:
What could not be read in it and is no artifact's: a folder that
cannot be listed, the ledger, its templates.

health.description:
How it stands as a whole, from everything below. A [`Listing`] read
for some kinds tells it from what it read of them, as it counts the
tally, and from `misplaced`, which no listing narrows: a skill that
does not read leaves `ok` a project listed for its rules. Reading
every kind for the health alone was the other way, which would weigh
a failure the listing says nowhere.

id.description: The id its settings name it by (D-09), which a move is followed by.

marker.description:
The file its marker is read from, which says an older one `mind
migrate` moves.

migrates.description:
Whether `mind migrate` has it to move: an older marker marks it, a
`mind.toml` or a `settings.json`, whose settings nothing but that
move changes ([`MindProject::changeable`]); false for an entry that
opens no project. Told here rather than by a front end comparing
`marker` with the file it knows to be the newest, which would be the
rule written again, and wrong once a newer one is.

misplaced.description: Each folder its settings name in `targets` that no install uses.

missed.description:
Each rule it received that some of its agents read nowhere, and
each MCP server it received that some of them are given no entry
of, as `status` says them.

name.description: What its marker calls it; none for an entry that opens no project.

settings.description:
What its settings say, which a change of them starts from; none for
a project a `mind.toml` marks, which has none to change.

stale.description:
Why its entry opens no project, when it does not: listed rather than
left out, since it is the one somebody has to find to unlink it.

tally.description: How many of them are of each kind, and stand in each state.

templates.description: What `mind add --template` can start from in it.

unreached.description:
Each kind it installs only where some of its agents do not read, as
`status` says it.

ProjectId.description: A project's id: 128 random bits, written as 32 lowercase hexadecimal digits.

ProjectSettings.description: What a project's settings say, as a change of them takes it.

agents.description:
Its agents, in the order its settings name them, which a change
keeps for the ones it keeps: not report order, which
[`Project::agents`] is in.

targets.description:
Each kind it names `targets` for, in report order: none when every
kind goes where its agents read.

ProjectUpdates.description: One project's installations an update says something of.

entry.description: The entry, as the registry spells it, which a task names it by.

installations.description: Each of them, by kind and then name.

writes.description: Whether updating the project writes something.

Ran.description:
What one write did: the lines it was, and what running them produced.

What a run is answered with, and each entry of the transcript: named as
its route's answer is ([`Answer::Ran`](crate::Answer::Ran)), rather than
as an entry, which a description of the API would put beside the
ledger's.

lines.description: The command lines, each as somebody would type it.

outcome.description:
What running them produced: the backend's
[`Outcome`](crate::Backend::Outcome), as its JSON, carried unread.

Reason.description:
The rule that chose a workspace: named on the command line,
activated for the shell, found walking up, or the default in home.

Refused.description:
What every answer under `/api` that is no success holds, whoever turned
the request away, the server or the backend: `{"code": "...", "error":
"..."}`, an object of these two fields and no other.

One type for both ([`error`], [`refused_by`]) rather than an object
spelled where each is answered, so the shape a script reads every
refusal by is said once.

code.description:
The one word a script acts on, which never changes when the words
are made clearer: a [`Condition`]'s, or the backend's own.

error.description:
What happened, for a person: the route, the parameter or the header,
what was expected and what came.

Run.description:
What one command line produced, as a terminal would show it, with the
code of everything that went wrong beside its words.

command.description: The line, as it would be typed into a shell ([`shell`]).

error.description: Why it could not run, when it could not.

ok.description:
Whether it ran and found everything in order: what its exit status
would have said.

stderr.description:
Each line it said on stderr, with its code; none for a hint or a
note, which no code is given to.

Running.description:
What an agent runs or reaches, as a front end shows it: whether it is
an address rather than a program, and the line, as [`Runs`] displays
it, each word a shell would split quoted.

The line as core writes it rather than the words for a front end to
join, which would be the shell's quoting spelled again in TypeScript,
and could show a line no shell reads as the program it is.

line.description: The program as a shell line that runs it, or the address.

reaches.description:
Whether it reaches an address, which it then is, rather than
starting a program.

Said.description:
An error as a serialized type holds one: its code, for a front end to act
on, and its message, for whoever reads it.

Built where the type is serialized, or kept in what a front end reads
(the workspace's snapshot), in place of the error, since an error
holds what JSON has no shape for (an `io::Error`, a parser's own), and
only these two are meant to leave core. Its fields are public for a
front end that reads the snapshot as Rust rather than as JSON, the TUI.

message.description:
Written through [`redacted`](crate::url::redacted), as every URL
is: an error can quote one, a source's among them, and what built
the error is no promise that it carries no credential.

ScanReason.description:
Why a directory a scan found is worth linking, the strongest of what
it holds, best first: a mind project its settings name by an id, one
with none, a git repository an agent reads something in, and any
other git repository.

Scanned.description:
What a scan the panel asked for found ([`Query::Scan`]): what `mindweaver
scan --suggest --json` prints, each directory with what the panel needs
to offer it, and what the command warns of beside it.

A shape of the backend's rather than the envelope the command prints,
since what it adds to each directory is a front end's: the words the
command says why in, what marking it asks for, and the entry a relink
names. Each worked out here, in Rust, where the minds screen works out
the same, rather than by the panel from the scan's fields.

depth.description: How many levels below each root it looked.

found.description:
Every directory it found, in the order `mindweaver scan --suggest` ranks
them: what is not linked first, most worth linking first, then what
is.

roots.description:
Where it looked, each once, in the order given: the workspace's root
when it was given none.

truncated.description:
Whether it stopped at core's bound before looking everywhere, which
`warnings` says too.

untraced.description:
Each entry where no project is any more whose id the ledger never
learned, as the scan spells it: what `mindweaver relink <entry> <path>`
follows, which only somebody who knows where it went can type.

warnings.description:
What it could not read, and that it stopped early, as `mindweaver scan`
warns of them, each with its code.

Selected.description:
What `POST /api/v1/plan` is sent: the boxes of projects and offers,
ticked or not, whose plan it answers with ([`Query::Plan`]).

Share.description:
Whether what is installed into a project reaches the team, as the
settings file and `mind share` spell it.

ShelfSource.description:
A source the shelf is filled from, with what `--from` takes for what it
supplied, how much of it the shelf holds and since when: a row of
`mindweaver gather sources` (#100), as the snapshot lists it too.

Counted and dated here, from the shelf's rows, rather than by a front
end from [`Snapshot::shelf`], as every count a view shows is. `shelved`
and `gathered_at` were added after the rest, which moved no version.

directory.description:
The folder this source owns under `.mindweaver/<kind folder>/`.

Stored rather than derived: two URLs can reduce to the same readable
name, and where a source's files went is a fact about the past that
must not move when the naming rule changes.

entry.description:
What the plugin is called in its marketplace's catalog, for one
gathered from a marketplace: what it is, as `--plugin` takes it,
where its URL and its folder are only where the catalog says it is
today. `None` for every other source.

gathered_at.description:
When its last gather put on the shelf what it holds there, in
seconds since the Unix epoch: the latest of their `gathered_at`, a
gather recording every artifact it takes, changed or not. `None`
while the shelf holds nothing of it.

name.description:
What it is called (D-13), one name a source: `owner-repo` unless
somebody named it ([`SourceName::derived`]), what a listing shows
and `--from` takes.

origin.description:
[`Source::origin`], which every artifact it supplied is installed
from.

parent.description:
What the marketplace listing it is called, for a plugin gathered
from one (D-13): the source a refresh or a removal of it goes
through, as `gather sources` shows it. `None` for every other.

pin.description:
The commit its last gather was pinned to (`gather git --pin`, #99),
which its `revision` is then: `None` while it follows its branch,
or the remote's HEAD. Not part of what the source is: moving the
pin, or gathering it with none, gathers into the same source.

reference.description:
The branch or tag asked for, or `None` for whatever the remote's HEAD
points at.

revision.description: The commit last gathered from, once one has been resolved.

shelved.description:
How many of its artifacts the shelf holds, of each kind it holds
any of, in report order: none for a source no gather has put
anything on the shelf from.

subdirectory.description:
The folder inside the source that was harvested: `.`, the whole
repository, by default, and `skills` for a source an older build
registered with what was its default then.

url.description:
The URL as the user typed it, without the credentials [`redacted`]
takes out.

Shelved.description:
One artifact gathered onto the shelf, with what `--from` takes for it.

The ledger's row with its origin beside it, as `gather list --json`
prints an offer from the shelf: the same names, so a script reading
either reads one shape. Beside the row rather than in it, since an offer
flattens the row beside an origin of its own.

content_hash.description:
[`crate::hash::tree`] of what was put on the shelf, the recipe an
install keeps of its copies: whether the shelf still holds what was
gathered, and whether two gathers took the same thing.

gathered_at.description: When it was gathered, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

How each entry in the registry stands with every offer, in the
order `projects` lists them: what each of its boxes shows.

the snapshot ([`Machine`]).

healths.description:
Every health a project can be in, in report order: what a front end
sorts and filters its projects by, so it orders none of its own.

history.description: The latest actions, newest first, at most [`HISTORY`].

kinds.description:
Every kind this build knows, in report order: what a front end lays
its columns out by, so a kind added to core reaches it without a

known.description:
Every workspace this machine knows ([`crate::known`]), this one

loaded.description: Every workspace it loads, in the order its marker lists them.

offers.description:
Everything there is to install, from wherever it is offered: what

projects.description:

shelf.description: Everything gathered onto its shelf, by kind, then name, then source.

sources.description: Every source the shelf is filled from, by URL.

states.description: Every state an artifact can stand in, in report order.

projects holding one id, what a loaded workspace cannot offer, a
ledger whose shelf or history would not read.

Source.description:

entry.description:

where its URL and its folder are only where the catalog says it is

What it is called (D-13), one name a source: `owner-repo` unless

and `--from` takes.

parent.description:
What the marketplace listing it is called, for a plugin gathered
from one (D-13): the source a refresh or a removal of it goes
through, as `gather sources` shows it. `None` for every other.

pin.description:
The commit its last gather was pinned to (`gather git --pin`, #99),
which its `revision` is then: `None` while it follows its branch,
or the remote's HEAD. Not part of what the source is: moving the

revision.description: The commit last gathered from, once one has been resolved.

The folder inside the source that was harvested: `.`, the whole
repository, by default, and `skills` for a source an older build

url.description:
The URL as the user typed it, without the credentials [`redacted`]

What a run under way is doing, as one word: each step of a gather, in
the order it takes them, then a backup's that are not a gather's, then a
search's.

oneOf.description: Reaching the source, before it has sent anything.
Receiving the objects it sends.
Resolving the deltas among them.

Writing the fetched revision's files into the clone; for a backup,

Reading the folders that hold a manifest.
Putting what was read on the shelf.

Once somebody approves the project's servers when it asks; a run
with no one to ask starts them all the same.
Only in a project its user's config marks trusted.
With nothing asked.

State.description: How an artifact stands in a project, as `status` says it.

One step of a run under way, as the panel is told it: what the run is
doing, how far it has got, the same in the words a terminal draws it
in, and whether a cancel asked now still stops it.

What the panel's backend reports through the server (`progress`), as
the server carries it unread: its words and its verdict worked out
here, from core's step, so the panel draws a bar and offers a cancel
without spelling a step, nor the point past which a cancel comes too
late, in TypeScript. Of no one run's shape but its stages: a gather's
and a backup's checking out, exporting, committing and pushing are
said in the same five fields, a backup's with no count.

cancellable.description:
Whether a cancel asked now still stops the run, as core says of
the step (`Progress::cancellable`): true until a gather starts
putting what it read on the shelf, and until a backup starts
pushing.

done.description: How much of it is done, when the stage counts anything.

said.description:
The step in words, as `mindweaver gather` draws it on a terminal
and the TUI in its box ([`said`]): `receiving objects 120/340`.

stage.description: What it is doing, as one word.

total.description: Of how much, once that is known.

Suggestion.description: One directory a scan found, and what the panel offers for it.

moved_from.description:
The entry it moved from, as the marker spells it, which a relink
names: matched by core's `scan::moved_from`, as the minds screen
matches it, since the scan spells `moved` as `mindweaver link` would
take it. None when it did not move.

offers.description:
What marking it asks for ([`MindsChange::of_found`]): linking it, or
making it a project first. None for one linked, and for one found
moved, which wants a relink rather than a second entry beside the one
it left stale.

why.description:
Why it is worth linking, in the words `mindweaver scan --suggest` and the
minds screen say it in ([`worth_linking`]); none for one linked.

Summary.description:
What a workspace holds, counted: the projects it links, those that open
none, and the artifacts its projects, its library and its shelf hold.

Counted here rather than by a front end from the lists beside it, for
the reason a [`Tally`] is, and because a count of projects is no list's
length: two entries can spell one directory.

held.description: What those projects hold together, each project once.

library.description: What its library holds: its own, which stand in no state.

projects.description:
How many directories its registry names that open a project: each
once, however many entries spell it, as [`KnownWorkspace::projects`]
counts them.

shelf.description: What its shelf holds, which stands in no state either.

stale.description: How many it names that open none, each once.

Switch.description:
What the panel asks to switch to: a workspace by its path, as the
answer to [`Query::Workspaces`] lists it, `{"path": "/home/you/work"}`.

A path matched against that list, read again when the switch arrives,
and never opened as sent ([`policy::switched`]): a browser goes to no
workspace that list does not offer. A field it does not have is
refused, as a task's is.

Switchable.description:
A workspace a front end that stays on one may switch to, as
[`switchable`] lists it: the row `mindweaver workspaces` prints, with how it
stands with the front end.

Beside the row rather than in it, as [`crate::view::KnownHere`] stands
beside it: the row is the machine's list, the same whoever asks, and
which one a front end was launched on is the front end's.

default.description:
The default workspace, in home: listed for being the default,
whatever its own `known` says.

in_use.description: The one in use where the list was asked for, as `resolve` chose it.

launched.description: Whether it is the one the front end was launched on.

name.description:
What its marker calls it; none for one that would not open, which has
no marker to read.

projects.description:
How many projects it links, each directory once, stale ones among
them: its own count, which says which of several weavers is which.

reason.description:
The rule it is chosen by once switched to, as a snapshot of it says:
the launch's, for the one the front end was launched on, and named,
as `-W` names it, for every other, since a switch names it to every
line the front end runs from then on, and nothing else chose it.

Whether the default workspace's `known` names it, which is what

stale.description:
Why it would not open, when it would not: listed rather than left
out, since a workspace that has gone is the one somebody has to find
to forget it.

Written through [`redacted`](crate::url::redacted), as an error's
message is in a [`Said`](crate::code::Said): a marker that does not
parse is quoted in its own words, a source's URL among them perhaps,

stale_projects.description: How many of those would not open.

switchable.description:
Whether a switch to it is offered: it opens, it is not the one in

How many artifacts a holder holds of each kind, and how many of them

is, and the panel counting its own would be a second set of them.

kinds.description:
How many of each kind it was read for, in report order, one it holds
none of among them: what a front end lays a column a kind out by.

states.description:
How many stand in each state, every state in report order, one none
stands in among them. A row that stands in none, the library's own
or one whose only copy does not read, is in no count here.

Task.description:
Work a front end asked for, as the command it is.

In JSON, what the panel sends to be run, each variant is an object
tagged by its name in snake_case, its fields beside the tag: `{"type":
"link", "path": "beta"}`. Tagged inside the object rather than around
it, so a task reads as one flat record, the shape TypeScript tells a
union apart by. A field a task with fields does not have is refused
rather than passed over, as one its holder or its agents line does not
have is: a task is a write, and one sent with a field misspelled would
run without it. Each name is a contract once a front end sends it, as a
report's is, so a test pins every one.

oneOf.description: `mindweaver init`, where the TUI was opened.
`mind init`, where the TUI was opened.
`mindweaver link <path>`.
`mind link`: the project the TUI is on, into the workspace above it.
`mind -C <path> init`, then `mindweaver link <path>`.
`mindweaver unlink <entry>`.

`mindweaver relink <old> <new>`: a stale entry pointed at where the scan
found its project, moved.
`mindweaver load <path>`.
`mind load <path>`: into the workspace above the project the TUI is on.
`mindweaver unload <entry>`.

`mind unload <path>`: out of the workspace above the project the TUI
is on, by its absolute path, which reads the same from anywhere.

`… add [--template <template>] <kind> <name> <description>`, or,
for an MCP server, `… add mcp <name> <description>` and the options
that say how an agent starts it or reaches it (`server`): what the
panel's form adding one sends, the form's fields as the options'
words, each secret the name of the variable it is read from.

server.description:
None but for a server added from its options, which a template
says otherwise: the grammar refuses both, and so the line does.

oneOf.description: `… show <kind:name>`.

`… edit <kind:name>`, which hands the terminal to an editor until it is
closed.

`mindweaver edit [-p <project>] --contents <file> --if-unchanged <hash>
<kind:name>`: what the artifact is read from, a skill's `SKILL.md`
or a rule's file, replaced with `text` whole, only while it holds
what `hash`, the SHA-256 the panel was given with what it read
(`contents::Contents::hash`), is the hash of.

The text, never a path: the file the line reads is the workspace's
scratch file for it ([`scratch_route`]), named by the line, which
the front end running it writes the text into before the line runs
and takes away after. A front end that has not written it runs a
line that reads nothing, which `edit` says. The workspace's command
at either level, `-p` naming a project, rather than `mind -C`, so
the route is read from the workspace's root, where the lines run and
the scratch folder is.

`… edit mcp:<name>` and the options that say how an agent starts
the server or reaches it: its transport and inputs written again
from them, everything else its definition holds kept
(`lifecycle::retransport`). What the panel's form changing one
sends, as the form adding one sends `add`'s.
`… rename <kind:name> <to>`.

`… remove --yes <kind:name>`: asked about before it gets here, which is
what the `--yes` says. `mindweaver remove --everywhere --yes <kind:name>`
when `everywhere`, one of the workspace's own taken out of every
project it links first. Without `yes`, the dry run, which deletes
nothing and says what would go, each project's copy with how it
stands when `everywhere`: what the panel shows before it asks.
`mindweaver validate`, everything; `mind validate`, one project.

`mind -C <path> init` for each repository that is not a project yet,
then one `mindweaver link` and one `mindweaver unlink`: what the minds screen's
marks amount to, built from them by [`Task::minds`].

What a front end's marks on directories ask for, each by the path a
command is given: the batch [`Task::minds`] builds from them, whose
lines these are, as the minds screen's are.

How the panel links what a scan found: it sends its marks, never the
batch, so that a directory made a project is then linked, with the
rest, by the one function that says so, and the same marks make the
same lines on either front end: the same words where both spell a
folder alike, and the same batch folder for folder inside the
workspace, where the panel names one by its path, all the path
policy takes, and the minds screen by its route from the root.
[`Minds`](Task::Minds) taken from a
browser was the other way, which would hold the panel to spelling
that rule again in TypeScript, and could leave a folder made a
project and never linked.
`mindweaver gather list`.

`mindweaver workspaces`: the workspaces this machine knows, the one in
use marked, to read.

`mindweaver gather search [--finder-url <finder>=<url>]... --json
<query>`: the skill directories the workspace enables asked what
they find, read back from the JSON the line prints, for a front end
to list and take one from with a [`Gather`](Task::Gather) of its
repository and its folder (#108), or, from the panel, a
[`TakeSkill`](Task::TakeSkill) of it.

No token, nor the name of a variable holding one: a front end hands
none over (D-16), so the line asks no finder that needs one, GitHub's
code search, and says so. JSON, since what a front end takes is what
it reads, by the names the envelope's `data` gives each result, never
a table's columns read back. Each finder at its own address, unless
the front end was told another where it was started ([`Catalogs`]):
the task names none.

`mindweaver gather git [--path <folder>] [--ref <branch>]
<repository>`: a skill a search of the skill directories found
([`SearchSkills`](Task::SearchSkills)), gathered from its repository
and its folder there, at the branch a finder named, by the line
`gather search --take` amounts to ([`Task::taking`]).

What the panel sends to take a result it listed: the result as the
search's JSON gave it, sent back whole, never a gather it puts
together, so which folder a result naming none is gathered from, and
which kind a take gathers, are said by the one function the TUI's
take and `--take` follow too, never again in TypeScript, as the
panel's marks are turned into lines by [`Task::minds`]. Its
repository is held to the path policy as a gather's source is, and
it carries no token, as a gather's task carries none.

`mindweaver gather mcp search [--registry <url>] --json <query>`:
the official MCP Registry asked for the servers whose name holds the
query, read back from the JSON the line prints, by the names the
envelope's `data` gives each server, for a front end to list and add
one from with an [`ImportServer`](Task::ImportServer) (#107).

The official registry, as the command asks unless told another, or
the mirror the front end was told where it was started
([`Catalogs`]): a task names no registry, so a browser sends no
address for a line to ask and take a program from.

`mindweaver gather mcp add [--registry <url>] [--version <version>]
[--yes] <server>`: the official registry's server, or the front
end's mirror's ([`Catalogs`]), by the name it gives it, written
into the workspace's library as a definition with `yes`; without
it the dry run, which writes nothing and says what an agent would
run or reach, what a front end shows before it asks for the yes.
Nothing is started either way. The latest version unless `version`
names one.

`mindweaver gather git [--kind <kind>] [--path <folder>] [--ref <ref>]
<url>`.

`kind` is what is taken, skills unless it says rules, as the
command's `--kind` is: added after the rest (#111), and skills when
a task leaves it out, as one sent before it was there does. The line
leaves out the folder only when it is the one a gather of the kind
looks in unsaid (`gather::default_folder`), so a task of rules from
the whole repository says `--path .`, which core asks of a gather of
rules.

`mindweaver gather marketplace --list --json [--ref <ref>] <source>`:
a plugin marketplace's catalog, Claude Code's or Codex's, recorded as
a source and its plugins listed, none gathered, read back from the
JSON the line prints, for a front end to list the plugins and gather
the ones ticked with a [`GatherPlugins`](Task::GatherPlugins) (#103,
#104).

Followed as it goes and stopped when asked, as a gather is
([`Followed::Gather`]): it fetches the catalog's repository. No
token, as a gather's task carries none.

`mindweaver gather marketplace [--ref <ref>] --plugin <name>...
<source>`: the plugins of a plugin marketplace called `plugins`
in its catalog gathered, each as a source of its own, in the order
given (#103). Never `--all`, which a front end asks for by naming
every plugin it lists, so the line says what was gathered.

`mindweaver gather update <name>...`: each source named gathered
again, as it was gathered, or every one, `--all`, when `names` is
empty. Followed as it goes and stopped when asked, as a gather is
([`Followed::Gather`]), and carrying no token, as a gather's task
carries none.

`mindweaver gather remove [--yes] <name>`: the source called `name`
forgotten, what it put on the shelf and its clone taken away, and
what was installed from it left orphaned, which is asked about first
([`Caution::Forgets`]). Without `yes`, the dry run, which says what
would go and writes nothing.

`mindweaver export [--kind <kind>]... [--yes] <folder>`: the
workspace's own written into `folder`, laid out as a workspace of
their own, `kinds` alone when it names some and every kind when it
names none. Without `yes`, what adds is written and what would
change or remove what an earlier export wrote there is only said;
with it, `--yes`, which takes that away, and is asked about first
([`Caution::Removes`]).

`mindweaver backup [--branch <branch>] [--kind <kind>]... [--message
<message>] [--token-env <variable>] <url>`: that export made into a
check-out of the repository at `url`, committed and pushed, on
`branch` or the repository's own, with `message` or the command's.

`token_env` is the name of an environment variable of whatever runs
the line, the panel's server or the TUI, holding a token, never a
token: a front end enters no credential, nor sends one (D-16), and
the command reads the variable for the one run. Without it, `git`
logs in as it is configured to. Followed as it goes and stopped
when asked until it pushes ([`Followed::Backup`]).

`… targets set --yes <kind> <dir>...`, or `… targets reset --yes
<kind>` when no folder is named: what the targets form amounts to.

`… agents --yes <agent>...`, then `… share --yes <mode>
[--edit-tracked]`, each only when what it sets changes: what the
agents and share toggles amount to.

agents.description: The agents to name, when they change.

share.description: The share mode, when it or `edit_tracked` changes.

oneOf.description:
What a project's toggles amount to, turned from `was`, what its
settings say, to `now`, what the toggles say: the
[`Settings`](Task::Settings) task [`Task::settings`] builds, whose
lines these are, as the TUI's toggles' are.

How the panel changes a project's agents and share mode: it sends
the toggles as they stand, never the lines' agents, so the order a
project names them in, and what unticking every one asks, is said by
the one function, never again in TypeScript. `was` is what the
panel read in the snapshot, as the TUI's is what it read when the
form opened: each line names the agents and the mode outright, so a
`was` the disk has moved on from changes which lines run, never what
a line sets.

`… update --yes [<kind:name>]`: what is installed in a project, or
the one artifact named, brought up to date and put back where a copy
has gone; `mindweaver update --all --yes [<kind:name>]` for the
workspace's own row, in every project it links. With `force`, `--yes
--force`, writing over a copy changed since it was installed too,
which the line is then asked about for ([`Caution::Forces`]).

`mindweaver install -p <project>... [--from <origin>] <kind:name>`: one
offer into each project named, by what picks it out
([`WeaverWorkspace::naming`]), from the place `from` names when it
names one.

Each of `projects` is what `naming` gives, an entry or a path from
the root, never a project's name, though `-p` takes one: a value
that starts with a dash reaches `-p` behind a `./` (`directory`),
which names the same directory, and so picks the same project by its
path, but is no longer a name `pick` would match. `-p=-odd`, which
would keep it a name, was the alternative, and it would change the
line the TUI has always run and shown for such a project.

With `yes`, `--yes`: an MCP server from elsewhere than the library
written ([`install::asks_first`]), once what each agent would run
has been shown, as the install screen shows it before it applies;
without, such a line writes nothing and says what it would.

In JSON for the panel's confirmation of such a server alone (#97):
a plan's task carries none ([`Task::from`]), and its confirmation,
shown beside what each agent would run, is the one task that does
([`Task::confirmed`], the backend's `Planned::asks`). A yes sent
with any other install is refused by the path policy before a line
is built (`policy::confirmed`, `install_yes_unasked`), and one left
out is none, as before a yes could be sent.

[`WeaverWorkspace::naming`]: mindweaver_core::WeaverWorkspace::naming
[`install::asks_first`]: mindweaver_core::install::asks_first

`mindweaver uninstall -p <project>... <kind:name>`: one artifact taken
back out of each project named, whichever place its copy came from,
each named as an install's are, by what `naming` gives. With
`force`, `--force`, taking out a copy changed since it was installed
too, which the line is then asked about for ([`Caution::Forces`]):
never from the install screen, whose marks leave an edit to a command
line, and from the panel only for the copy core says needs it.

`… uninstall --orphaned`: every installation in a project that
nothing offers any more where it came from, taken back out of it;
`mindweaver uninstall --all-projects --orphaned` for the workspace's own
row, out of every project it links, as an update reaches them. Never
forced: one changed since it was installed is left, every copy of it,
for a command line that says `--force` once somebody has looked.

`mindweaver adopt -p <project> --yes <kind:name>`: somebody's skill in
the project's agents' folders brought into the workspace's library,
its copies recorded as installed from there: asked about before it
gets here, which is what the `--yes` says. The project is named as an
install's are, by what `naming` gives.

`mindweaver migrate -p <project> [--yes]`: one project the workspace
links moved from an older marker, a `mind.toml` or a
`settings.json`, to a `settings.toml`, what the workspace records of
it carried along; without `yes`, the dry run, which writes nothing
and says what would move. The project is named as an install's are,
by what `naming` gives.

The workspace's command, as an install's is, so what it carries is
what the workspace on screen records: `mind migrate` in the project
finds a workspace by walking up, which misses one linking the
project from beside it. The agents and the share mode are left to
the command, every agent and shared for a `mind.toml`, as a project
committed by design was, and what a `settings.json` names for one,
for `mind agents` and `mind share` to change once it is moved.
Open the install screen, which is what `mindweaver install` opens.

What the install screen marked, as the `Install` and `Uninstall`
tasks it amounts to ([`Screen::task`]), each run whatever came
of the ones before.

info.description:
The HTTP API `mindweaver ui` serves, for scripts and tools on this machine as much as for the web panel, its first client. A read is a GET naming what it reads in its parameters, and a read that takes a structure a POST that changes nothing; every change is a task, the command lines it is, previewed and then run, so the API does nothing the command line cannot. A script that did not start the panel finds where the API is and its token in the file `mindweaver ui --token-file` writes. A route, a parameter or a field once served is a contract: dropping or renaming one, or changing what it holds, moves the API to `/api/v2`, and adding one does not, so an answer's schema leaves room for a field it does not name. Written from the Rust that serves it, never by hand.

Served on 127.0.0.1 alone, at the port the system chose unless one was named, every route behind the launch token, as a Bearer token or as the cookie the launch link sets. Every answer that is no success is a `Refused`, `{"code", "error"}`, its code the word a script acts on and its error the words a person reads: a path under `/api` no route names, of another version or of none, is a 404 of `unknown_route`. Every answer under `/api` carries `Cache-Control: no-store`, and none grants another origin the right to read it.
